relevance_note: The review reports individual-level SSADH deficiency data, e.g. "She has an Aldh5A1 mutation (p.Gly409Asp)." for the living sister of the postmortem case, so identifiable in-scope people with individual-level detail are described.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules. No script transcribed anything: Tables 1-5 of this paper are group counts (n, %) with no patient rows or columns, so nothing was transcribed positionally, and no cell in the paper contains the stacked-cell separator ' / ' (v6, D-31 not triggered). In scope: the 19-year-old deceased woman of the postmortem report and her living sister (both cited as '(Knerr et al 2008b)'), the 'two adolescent brothers' of Leuzzi et al 2007, the '2 1/2-year-old boy' of Saronwala et al 2008, the single patient of Arnulf et al 2005, and two patients of the authors' own NIH imaging protocol described individually ('One patient had asymmetric involvement of the globus pallidus...', 'In the oldest patient studied (age 27 years)...'); these two are the 7 patients minus the 5 symmetric ones. Out of scope (counts only, no rows): the 60-patient questionnaire database (Tables 1-2), the adolescent/adult patients (N=35, Tables 3-5), the 33 patients of Knerr et al 2008a, the 7 flumazenil-PET patients, the 10 polysomnography patients, the eight TMS families, the 'approximately 400 identified cases worldwide' and the 110 mild-cognitive-impairment patients. publications.cohort_size_as_stated = 60 (largest patient number the authors state for their own database). Contradiction found: the deceased woman's postmortem evaluation carried 'the assigned diagnosis of epilepsy of unknown aetiology' while the paper assigns her SSADH deficiency. Uncertainties: (1) the two sisters carry no printed label, so labels were made up under rules 6 and 2 ('unnamed person 1', 'sister of unnamed person 1'); (2) literature patients are labelled 'ref <author year> patient' because the text cites them as '(Leuzzi et al 2007)', '(Saronwala et al 2008)', '(Arnulf et al 2005)' and never by reference number; (3) the paper does not name the disease in the sentences about the Leuzzi brothers or the Arnulf patient, so disease_label_as_stated is 'not reported' for them (in-scope status rests on context: extrapyramidal manifestations of SSADH deficiency, and the SSADH sleep paragraph); (4) the deceased woman's 'seizure onset at age 13 years' was recorded as age_at_onset although her developmental delay has no stated age, and the diagnosis is only retrospective; (5) interpretation calls: 'the pallidal signal abnormality was subtle' was counted as the checklist item T2 hyperintensity of globus pallidus (paragraph context is T2 signal), 'borderline cognition (IQ = 70)' was NOT counted as intellectual disability, the boy's taurine-associated insomnia WAS counted as sleep disturbances, and the reference [21] title's 'paroxysmal dystonia' for the Leuzzi brothers was not used (the text says 'exercise-induced paroxysmal dyskinesias'), so dystonia is 'not reported' for them. No variant row was made for the deceased woman: the paper says 'Although DNA analysis on the decedent is in progress' and never ties a variant to her.
